title: TG#2 + TG#3 caption self-locating fields (camera, timestamp, alert number)
author: the operator
trigger: Operator observed (2026-09-12): after a vehicle drive-by they received TG#1 + TG#2 + TG#3 alerts but could not correlate them to a specific camera or event because TG#2 and TG#3 captions do not include camera name, event timestamp, or which alert-number this message is. TG#1's caption already includes Camera + Alert ID + Timestamp; TG#2 and TG#3 must be brought up to parity.
background: The v2 pipeline emits up to three Telegram messages per alert event: TG#1 (motion+gate, photos of composite+full-frame), TG#2 (YOLO-classified detail, photos of crop_a+crop_b), and TG#3 (vehicle-match result, text-only). TG#1's caption was standardized in commit 721bec5 to include 'Camera: <name>', 'Alert ID: <uuid>', and 'Timestamp: <iso>'. TG#2 (telegram_formatter/detail.py:build_detail_message) and TG#3 (telegram_formatter/match_alert.py:build_match_message) do not include those fields today. When the operator scrolls through Telegram later, the messages are individually ambiguous: which camera? which minute? which alert-number in the sequence? This PRD brings TG#2 and TG#3 to parity with TG#1 by adding the same three fields plus an alert-sequence label ('Alert 2 of 3' / 'Alert 3 of 3') so each message is self-locating in isolation.
shipping_definition: All US-033 stories marked done; pytest suite green (no regressions in existing test_alert_message_caption.py or test_pipeline.py); tree clean; on the next live alert event, the TG#2 caption includes the literal lines 'Camera: <name>', 'Alert 2 of 3', 'Alert ID: <uuid>', and 'Timestamp: <iso>'; the TG#3 caption includes the literal lines 'Camera: <name>', 'Alert 3 of 3', 'Alert ID: <uuid>', and 'Timestamp: <iso>'. The lines appear in that order, matching TG#1's caption layout. TG#1 caption is unchanged.
scope_exclusions: TG#1 caption changes are NOT this PRD (TG#1 already has Camera + Alert ID + Timestamp from 721bec5; operator explicitly only mentioned TG#2 and TG#3).
Re-architecting the message-dispatch pipeline (e.g. unifying TG#1/TG#2/TG#3 into a single builder) is NOT this PRD. The fix is local to the two existing builder functions.
Adding new fields beyond camera/timestamp/alert-number (e.g. weather, threat level, GPS) is NOT this PRD -- operator-locked: no threat fields anywhere (vision-prompt-design skill Rule 6).

Adding a per-camera webhook allowlist or new camera metadata sources is NOT this PRD. The fix only reads the fields already present on the alert dict (id, timestamp) and on the camera_label passed in from daemon.py.
Backfilling historical alerts (re-sending old TG#2/TG#3 messages with the new captions) is NOT this PRD. Only new alerts going forward.
Internationalization / locale formatting of timestamps is NOT this PRD. Pass through the alert['timestamp'] string verbatim.
Animal-mode TG#2 (mode='animal') is NOT in scope here even though build_detail_message accepts it. TG#3 is vehicle-only by design (animal TG#3 does not exist).
Cooldown logic / record_hit changes are NOT this PRD.
design_principles: Mirror TG#1: the new lines in TG#2 and TG#3 must use the exact same prefix strings and field order as TG#1 so the operator can read any of the three messages and parse them identically. TG#1's caption order (Camera, [mode-specific lines], Alert ID, Timestamp) is the template.

Alert-number label format: 'Alert 2 of 3' / 'Alert 3 of 3'. Literal string, not a count badge. TG#1 is already labeled 'Alert 1 of 3' conceptually but its caption does not include the label today; per operator rule 'TG#1 is not in this PRD' the label is NOT added to TG#1 in this PRD. (If operator wants TG#1 to also carry the label, file as a separate one-liner PRD.)

Field sourcing: camera_label comes from the existing parameter (TG#2 already receives it; TG#3 needs it added). alert_id and timestamp come from the alert dict -- pipeline.py already has the alert dict in scope at both build sites (TG#1 uses it today; TG#2 and TG#3 currently don't).
No new env vars or config. The fields are already present in the alert dict produced by listener/daemon.py:normalize_reolink() (line 186, 'timestamp': timestamp; line 181, 'id': str(uuid.uuid4())).

Pure-function builders: build_detail_message and build_match_message stay pure. The alert dict is passed in as a parameter, not read from globals or the daemon. Tests can construct an alert fixture and call the builder directly.

Backward compatibility: when alert is None (test fixtures that exercise the builders without a parent alert), the caption omits Alert ID and Timestamp lines. Existing tests that call build_detail_message without alert must continue to pass; this is the reason the alert parameter defaults to None. The same applies to build_match_message.
Single commit per story, per V2-032 pattern. Story body budget: 2500 chars per story.

Card body format: per orchestrator skill, write the body as a markdown bulleted list under 2500 chars that includes the goal, the ACs from the PRD, the files to touch, and a 'Verify' line with the exact pytest invocation.

stories.title: TG#2 caption: add Camera / Alert 2 of 3 / Alert ID / Timestamp lines
acceptance: telegram_formatter/detail.py:build_detail_message gains an optional alert parameter (dict | None, default None).

When alert is provided with id and timestamp, the caption includes the literal lines 'Alert 2 of 3', 'Alert ID: <id>', 'Timestamp: <timestamp>' in that order, after the existing Camera + Mode + Class confirmed lines and before any optional License plate / Distinctive features lines.

When alert is None (existing test fixtures), the caption does NOT include the Alert ID or Timestamp lines. Existing test_alert_message_caption.py tests that exercise build_detail_message without alert continue to pass unchanged.
Camera: line is unchanged -- already emitted from the existing camera_label parameter.
build_detail_message remains a pure function. No I/O, no network, no module-level state.

tests/test_alert_message_caption.py adds a test asserting the new lines appear (e.g. test_tg2_caption_includes_alert_metadata_when_alert_provided) and a test asserting the lines are absent when alert=None.
Single commit: 'TG#2 caption: add Camera / Alert 2 of 3 / Alert ID / Timestamp (US-033a)'.

stories.title: TG#3 caption: add Camera / Alert 3 of 3 / Alert ID / Timestamp lines
acceptance: telegram_formatter/match_alert.py:build_match_message gains two new required parameters: camera_label (str) and alert (dict | None, default None). Existing callers in pipeline.py are updated to pass camera_label=camera_label and alert=alert at the same call site (line ~187).

When alert is provided with id and timestamp, the caption includes the literal lines 'Alert 3 of 3', 'Alert ID: <id>', 'Timestamp: <timestamp>' in that order, after the Camera line and after the Status: recognized/unrecognized line.

When alert is None, the caption does NOT include the Alert ID or Timestamp lines. Existing callers that previously did not pass camera_label must be updated (pipeline.py:187 is the only call site in the repo).
Camera: line is the first line of the caption (before Status), matching TG#2's layout.
build_match_message remains a pure function. No I/O, no network, no module-level state.
tests/test_alert_message_caption.py adds a test asserting the new lines appear (test_tg3_caption_includes_alert_metadata_when_alert_provided) and a test asserting Camera line is first.
Single commit: 'TG#3 caption: add Camera / Alert 3 of 3 / Alert ID / Timestamp (US-033b)'.

stories.title: pipeline.py: thread alert dict into both TG#2 and TG#3 builders
acceptance: listener/pipeline.py:174 build_detail_message call gains an alert=alert keyword argument.
listener/pipeline.py:187 build_match_message call gains camera_label=camera_label and alert=alert keyword arguments.
The alert variable is the one already in scope at both call sites (the alert_dict that pipeline.run() received). No new variable, no dict copy.
Mode='animal' branch (TG#2 for animals) also passes alert=alert. The current code at pipeline.py:170-176 does not branch on mode, so this is automatic.
Single commit: 'pipeline: thread alert dict into TG#2/TG#3 builders (US-033c)'.

stories.title: integration test: pipeline.run() end-to-end emits TG#2/TG#3 with new fields
acceptance: tests/test_pipeline.py adds a test (test_pipeline_run_emits_self_locating_tg2_tg3_captions) that calls pipeline.run() with a fake alert dict containing id='evt-fake-001', camera_label='Front Gate', timestamp='2026-09-12T19:02:50.000+0000', classification='vehicle', and a small mock for VM1/VM2/match stages.
The test asserts the TG#2 dict's caption contains 'Camera: Front Gate', 'Alert 2 of 3', 'Alert ID: evt-fake-001', and 'Timestamp: 2026-09-12T19:02:50.000+0000'.
The test asserts the TG#3 dict's caption contains 'Camera: Front Gate', 'Alert 3 of 3', 'Alert ID: evt-fake-001', and 'Timestamp: 2026-09-12T19:02:50.000+0000'.
Single commit: 'test: TG#2/TG#3 self-locating caption integration test (US-033d)'.

open_questions_for_operator: Operator said 'OK in fact there's a bunch of problems with alerts two and three that we need to deal with'. This PRD only addresses the three named (camera, timestamp, alert-number). If the operator has additional TG#2/TG#3 problems (e.g. broken crop_a/crop_b paths, missing YOLO classification line, duplicate photo accumulation, etc.), file them as separate small stories in this PRD or as a follow-up PRD. Do NOT bundle unspecified problems into the camera/timestamp/alert-number work -- the operator's 'one directive, one scope' rule applies.
Should TG#1 ALSO get the 'Alert 1 of 3' label, or is it already obvious enough from being first? This PRD does not touch TG#1. Operator to decide if/when.

Should the alert-number label change wording? Current draft uses 'Alert 2 of 3' / 'Alert 3 of 3'. Operator may prefer 'TG#2' / 'TG#3' or 'Alert 2/3' or '(2/3)'. Worker should not change wording without operator approval -- file as a one-line follow-up if needed.
